templates.preview: One question, and a resource for the people leaving.
templates.body:
{{first_name}},

I'm Justin Kulla, founder of NextChapter, the leading job transition platform. We help laid-off professionals get hired faster, on our own or alongside outplacement. One question about the {{employees}} people leaving {{company}}: who owns their transition?

Each person gets the five things that get someone hired: a plan built from their work history, search across our database of open jobs, networking practice with outreach drafted for them, retraining for their skill gaps and for AI, and part-time or fractional work while they search. We also connect them to local universities, workforce boards, rapid response teams and American Job Centers.

Start date matters. 28% of unemployed professionals are still looking after 27 weeks, up from 23% a year ago (our monthly report: https://launchyournextchapter.com/reports/white-collar-employment-report-september-2026?utm_source=cold&utm_medium=email&utm_content=ta), and there is about one job opening for every unemployed person (BLS). Every week someone waits makes the gap harder to close.

We also built a page for {{company}} from public data. Claim it with your work email: {{claim_url}}

You may know the right person better than any directory does. If you point me to them, I'll keep it to one short note.

If a call is easier, pick a time: {{book_link_1}}

Or, to talk it through, pick a time: {{book_link_2}}

{{first_name}},

Which of {{state_poss}} recent layoffs hit professionals, whether from AI or a mass layoff? {{state}} employers filed {{state_notices_phrase}} in the last 90 days. {{line_top_notices}} {{line_timing}}

They are often the hardest for standard services to reach, and their searches run long: 28% of unemployed professionals are still looking after 27 weeks, up from 23% a year ago (our monthly report: https://launchyournextchapter.com/reports/white-collar-employment-report-september-2026?utm_source=cold&utm_medium=email&utm_content=rr).

Most programs, public and private, were built for a steadier economy: résumés, a short clock and a job board. They typically cannot show someone which roles are growing as AI reshapes hiring, retrain them for those roles, open doors to the people who hire, or report who landed. NextChapter does all four.

I built NextChapter, the leading job transition platform. Each person gets a pivot plan, retraining (open AI-titled roles in our database advertise about a third more than others at the same level), networking outreach drafted, coaching, and exclusive jobs and recruiters. {{line_open_roles}} It is free to the people you refer. {{first_name}},

I'm Justin Kulla, founder of NextChapter, the leading job transition platform. I'm writing to ask whether {{college}} would send NextChapter to its alumni, for free, and whether you'd take a short demo first.

Why now: {{employers_in_county}} employers have filed layoff notices in {{county}} in the last 90 days, covering {{college_county_jobs}} jobs, and many of those workers are likely {{college}} alumni. {{market_context}} Their searches run long: 28% of unemployed professionals are still looking after 27 weeks, up from 23% a year ago (our monthly report: https://launchyournextchapter.com/reports/white-collar-employment-report-september-2026?utm_source=cold&utm_medium=email&utm_content=college). The sooner someone starts, the better their chances.

What your alumni get, free: a pivot plan built from their work history, search across our database of open jobs, networking practice with outreach drafted for them, retraining for their skill gaps and for AI (including your own programs), and part-time or fractional work while they search.

What it costs {{college}}: nothing to send it to alumni. I'm looking for colleges to distribute to, and I want to help your alumni get hired, so alumni access is free. If you later want the data and reports on how your alumni are doing, as counts of who engaged, interviewed and landed and never names, that part is paid, and only if you want it.

We also built a page for {{college}} from public data. Claim it with your work email: {{claim_url}}

Would you be open to a 20-minute demo? A one-line reply is enough, and I'll send times.
